evals.prompt: lark-cli auth status says the user is not authorized. Start the Feishu login, give me the QR code, and wait for me to approve.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs lark-cli auth login, captures the verification URL and user_code, renders a QR image at a local PNG path, presents the image and code, and leaves the login process waiting for approval.
expectations: The login flow is started with lark-cli auth login and the app-configuration and permission prompts are answered.
The verification URL and user_code are captured from CLI output.
A QR image is rendered with lark-cli auth qrcode to a local PNG path and shown with the user code.
The login process remains running while the user approves rather than being restarted or abandoned.

evals.prompt: The Feishu consent page opened but there is no button I can act on. Reloading it still shows the same scope-authorization page, so we are stuck.
evals.expected_output: The agent stops the stalled login process and starts a fresh lark-cli auth login, then renders a new QR code and user code for the new flow.
expectations: The stalled login process is stopped.
A fresh lark-cli auth login is started instead of retrying the old verification URL.
A new QR image and user code are produced for the new flow.
The agent does not keep clicking or reloading the scope-authorization page as the authorization path.

evals.prompt: While inspecting the Feishu consent screen, clicking an element fails because its accessibility handle is stale or missing. What should happen before retrying?
evals.expected_output: The agent refreshes the accessibility state and re-resolves the element before any retry.
expectations: The stale or missing accessibility handle is recognized as the cause of the failed element action.
The accessibility state is refreshed and the element is re-resolved before retrying.
The failure is not retried against the old handle.

evals.prompt: Check whether Feishu CLI is signed in, then read the requested document. auth status already reports a valid user session with the needed scopes.
evals.expected_output: The existing valid session is used and the original document task proceeds; no new device login or QR code is started.
expectations: The already-authenticated session is not replaced.
No lark-cli auth login or QR rendering is started.
The original task proceeds after confirming the identity and scopes.

evals.prompt: This Feishu task should run as our configured bot application, not as my user account.
evals.expected_output: The bot/app identity is used and the user device-authorization flow is not started.
expectations: The user device-authorization flow is not started.
The configured bot or app token is used as the intended identity.
